task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Playoff defenses suppress DRIVE more than RS defenses; DRIVE allowed 1.191 -> 0.923 (-0.268), share 21.2% -> 18.2%; PNR -0.139, share +12.1pp; PULL_UP +0.341, share -7.6pp.

failed_approaches.why: No inferential test; PNR share jump of +12.1pp may reflect tagging differences; risk of LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR

evidence_establishes: Descriptive differences in PPP allowed for PULL_UP when PNR fails, but no statistical test of lift or threshold compliance.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lift>0.02 in ≥70% of units, the statistical significance of that lift, or causal inference of counter effect.
own_inferences: The available data provide per-game possession-level tags but the labeling of PNR and PULL_UP may be noisy; the sample of PNR-fail units may be sparse across seasons, limiting power.
uncertainties: Exact definition and consistency of PNR fail across seasons; potential systematic tagging errors; unknown distribution of units meeting the ≥70% criterion.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved study only offers descriptive evidence and highlights labeling and sample size risks, but does not alter the conclusion that the question remains untested.

blocking_constraints.text: Limited number of PNR-fail units across seasons may not provide enough power to detect a 2pp lift.
Potential labeling errors in PNR and PULL_UP tags.
Risk that PNR failures are misclassified due to tagging inconsistencies.
Few possessions per unit may lead to high variance in lift estimates.

prior_work.summary: Prior work described PPP differences for PULL_UP when PNR fails but did not conduct inferential testing of the lift threshold.

risks.text: Insufficient exposure of PNR-fail units across seasons.
PNR and PULL_UP labels may be inconsistent across datasets.
Other defensive factors (pace, opponent strength) may drive observed lift.
Low number of possessions per unit leads to high variance.

design.estimand: Average lift in points per 100 possessions of PULL_UP when PNR fails (≥0.02 threshold in ≥70% of units).
design.unit: team-game units where PNR fails in a possession.
design.sample: All PNR-fail units across 2022-26 seasons; aim for at least 200 units with ≥30 possessions each.
design.power: Target 80% power to detect 2pp lift at α=0.05; requires ~200 units with 30 possessions each (approx 6000 possessions).
design.controls: Include opponent defensive rating, pace, and game context (home/away).
design.falsification: Apply same lift test to units where PNR succeeds; expect lift ≈0.00 or negative. Also test on a placebo play type (e.g., DRIVE) to ensure specificity.
design.multiplicity: Adjust for multiple units with Holm–Bonferroni correction; report both per-unit and aggregate statistics.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if ≥70% of units show lift>0.02 and 95% CI excludes zero. Otherwise, fail to reject.
design.data_version: 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 regular season and playoffs up to 2026-06-21 (complete).
